text:
rachel: RFC follow-up: proposing a small "watchdog" around delta apply sequences for air-gapped installs. Want a quick sanity check on semantics and operator signals.

diego: Nice. What's the motivating failure mode? long partial applies? stuck mounts?

rachel: Exactly two issues we hit in staging: (1) large deltas sometimes hang in the middle (I/O/backpressure), leaving some components applied and others not, and (2) nodes occasionally flip network state during apply which screws up our finalization step. Need a guardrail that detects stuck applies and either rollbacks or moves to safe-staged state.

tom: Please propose concrete state machine. Without that it's hard to reason about operator UX.

rachel: Draft state machine: APPLY -> WATCHDOG -> STAGED -> RECONCILE -> ACTIVATE -> CLEANUP. WATCHDOG monitors progress and enforces checkpoints. If checkpoint misses X times, transition to QUARANTINE (no automatic rollback) OR AUTO_ROLLBACK depending on config.

elena: We should define 'checkpoint' precisely. Propose: every N bytes written or every component boundary we write a signed checkpoint record: {manifest_id, component_id, offset, checksum, timestamp}. Checkpoints get appended to /var/lib/redwood/apply-checkpoints.log and mirrored into last-successful-manifest when fully completed.

verifier-bot: note: signature policy: checkpoints must be signed by agent key; if signature verification fails during reconcile the node must go to QUARANTINE.

diego: What's X? 3 missed checkpoints? 2? Also what are reasonable defaults for big models vs small components?

rachel: defaults suggestion: checkpoint_interval_bytes=64MB, checkpoint_interval_components=1, watchdog_miss_threshold=3, watchdog_check_interval_ms=5000. These are tunable per-deployment.

tom: Good. For large model sharded files we may want smaller checkpoint bytes (32MB) because chunk retransfer cost is high. Suggest per-bundle override in bundle header.

elena: Important: we must ensure checkpoints are idempotent and replay-safe. If apply restarts we should be able to resume from last checkpoint by re-validating checksums for already-applied offsets and skipping. That implies component writers must support resume semantics.

rachel: Agree. Implementation note: write to a staging dir /var/lib/redwood/staged/<bundle_id>/parts and create a .marker file per-part once checksum verified. Then reconcile walks markers.

ops-bot: apply job 4155002222 status=started bundle=b-2026-05-02

diego: Operator UX: when watchdog trips, what should console show? Immediate reason, last checkpoint, and suggested action. Also a single-button action: 'rollback to last-success' or 'continue-resume'.

elena: On the console we should show a compact timeline and allow grabbing the staged tarball via one-click (scp) or pushing to masked mirror. Also include a 'force-resume' option that requires explicit acknowledgement and a typed confirmation.

tom: What about activation fencing? I want to avoid split-brain where two nodes think they're active because activation was partially applied during a network partition.

rachel: Activation fencing plan: the central control plane (for dedicated/private) or local leader election (for fully air-gapped) must manage an activation_token. Activation requires acquiring a token lease in a small on-disk store that is monotonically-incremented (lease_epoch). Activation records: {node_id, lease_epoch, manifest_id, activated_at, signature}. Nodes must refuse to activate if their manifest_id != latest manifest pinned in lease.

elena: For offline installs, the lease store can be implemented as a single-file monotonic counter under /var/lib/redwood/activation-lease when operator locks it via admin action. We must ensure activation is atomic: write temp -> fsync -> rename. Document that operators must place the lease file on a shared mount if multiple nodes share activation responsibility.

diego: How to handle recovery if lease store corrupted? fallback to manual operator intervention only. Paging thresholds: lease corruption -> page immediately.

verifier-bot: telemetry suggestions: watchdog_tripped_count, last_checkpoint_offset, activation_lease_epoch, activation_blocked_reasons.

rachel: Add a small CLI snippet for operators: 
```
# inspect checkpoints
redwood-agent checkpoints --bundle b-2026-05-02 --tail 50
# force rollback to last-known good manifest (opt-in flag required on node)
redwood-agent rollback --to-last-success --confirm
# attempt resume (requires typed confirmation)
redwood-agent resume --bundle b-2026-05-02 --force
```

tom: Also document the hazard of enabling auto-rollback on nodes that have local state changes that can't be reconstructed. Default should be conservative (no auto rollback).

elena: Agreed. We'll make auto_rollback=false by default and have a per-cluster policy for critical fleets. Add an alert when auto_rollback=true so operators know risk.

diego: One last thought: add a lightweight 'watchdog-dry-run' flag for new bundles so we can exercise logic in staging: the agent simulates checkpoint misses and reports expected transitions without changing state. Useful for QA.

rachel: Nice. I'll add that. Thanks for the quick bikeshed. I'll update the RFC with the state machine diagram, the checkpoint format, default knobs, a sample activation-lease spec, and the small operator CLI runbook. If no objections I'll land the follow-up and add a console mock for the timeline.

ops-bot: apply job 4155002222 status=watchdog:event=checkpoint_ok offset=67108864

rachel: merging follow-up later today unless someone objects.
